title: ChaCha Remote Operator MCP — self-hosted governed remote operations
problem: ChaCha DEV currently depends on a third-party remote terminal/filesystem connector whose commercial monthly call quota can halt otherwise authorized platform work even though the user's own VPS remains available.
goals: Provide a self-hosted MCP remote-operations endpoint controlled by ChaCha DEV.
Replace quota-dependent remote terminal, file, process, service and Git inspection workflows with a zero-license-cost capability.
Preserve Guardian, Sentinelle, Bastion, canonical STOP, append-only evidence and zero automatic external spend.
Start read-only and fail closed; add writes and destructive operations only through separately qualified governed profiles.
Support future multi-target operation across ChaChaVPS, ChaChaNas and ChaChaTel.
Use an open MCP transport so the backend is not tied to one conversational client.
non_goals: Do not expose an unrestricted root shell over the network.
Do not expose credentials, SSH private keys, tokens or secret stores through MCP tools.
Do not enable destructive filesystem, service, package-manager or production deployment operations in V0.1.
Do not bypass Guardian, Sentinelle, Bastion or canonical STOP.
Do not auto-purchase hosting, identity, tunnel or SaaS services.
Do not build graphical remote desktop control before terminal/filesystem operations are proven insufficient.

current_change.purpose: Create the read-first Streamable HTTP MCP foundation with bounded tools, path allowlisting, STOP enforcement and append-only audit.

acceptance_criteria: The server binds to localhost by default and exposes MCP Streamable HTTP at /mcp.
Health, system status, process list, file read, directory list, bounded search and service status tools work without shell interpolation.
Every path is resolved and rejected unless it is under an allowlisted root.
Canonical STOP blocks all operational tools when active.
Every tool call creates an append-only audit record without recording credentials or secret values.
Arbitrary command execution is disabled by the default V0.1 policy.
Destructive operations and production mutations are absent from the V0.1 tool surface.
A later write-enabled profile requires a separate qualification and explicit production approval.
architecture_invariants: GitHub remains the source-code and CI authority.
ChaCha DEV on ChaChaVPS remains the runtime orchestrator.
ChaChaNas remains the preferred durable persistence target when available.
MCP transport and machine-operation policy remain separate layers.
Producer and verifier responsibilities remain separated.
No network exposure is permitted before authentication and Bastion review are qualified.
